answers.q1: Yarn 1 (classic), pinned as yarn@1.22.22 in package.json. It's a yarn workspaces monorepo, so don't use npm or pnpm. Install dependencies with: yarn install
answers.q2: yarn test:app --watch=false. This runs vitest once and exits. Plain `yarn test` or `yarn test:app` starts vitest in watch mode. CI runs `yarn test:app`. The repo's own aggregate script is `yarn test:all`, which also runs typecheck, eslint and prettier.
answers.q4: These are the commands from .github/workflows/lint.yml, run in this order after `yarn install`: yarn test:other && yarn test:code && yarn test:typecheck. `test:other` is prettier --list-different on css, scss, json, md, html and yml files. `test:code` is eslint --max-warnings=0 --ext .js,.ts,.tsx . and `test:typecheck` is tsc. To auto-fix, run `yarn fix`.
answers.q5: Don't hand-edit yarn.lock or dev-docs/yarn.lock; AGENTS.md lists both as lockfiles. Don't edit installed or build output either: node_modules/, build/, dist/ (including excalidraw-app/build, excalidraw-app/dist and packages/*/dist), dev-dist, coverage, public/workbox, packages/excalidraw/types, and examples/**/public. These are all listed in .eslintignore. I did not check whether other files, such as the non-English locale files, are generated.

q1.reason: Yarn classic with `yarn install` matches the accept criterion and nothing contradicts the truth.

q2.reason: `yarn test:app --watch=false` is an accepted one-shot form, and the extra detail about CI and test:all is accurate.

q3.reason: `yarn vitest run packages/element/tests/bounds.test.ts` exactly matches an accepted command.

q4.reason: Gives yarn test:other, test:code and test:typecheck as CI does; the `yarn fix` mention is only an extra note, not the sole answer.

q5.reason: Names yarn.lock and build output dirs (build/, dist/, dev-dist, packages/excalidraw/types), matching the accept criterion; it admits not checking locales but that is not required.
